## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c337540fa983bdd2dc1a8fa3d2f6506cb33e4f7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: yes

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is one file, one hunk, one table row: `AGENTS.md`, Context Routing, the `packages/services/**` row (+1 −1). No code, schema, gate, test or generated file changes.
- Accept-set: unchanged. No validator, parser or gate reads this row, so nothing is accepted or refused differently. Right.
- Public surface: unchanged. `AGENTS.md` ships in no package and no export, route or CLI surface moves. Right.
- Agent-facing rule: one route changes. After a merge that creates a package whose name differs from an ADR's proposal, the landing seat no longer files its own `domain:skills` card for the ADR amendment; it adds one row to the open "ADR revisions, week of …" card, and opens next week's card when none is open. The first half of the clause (an ADR package name is a proposal, the PR follows the tree's precedent and leaves `docs/adr/**` untouched) is byte-identical apart from where its citation sits. Right: this is the change the card asks for, and it matches the rule already on `main` in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md` line 109 to 111.
- Byte budget: `AGENTS.md` on `main` is 78306 bytes and the row grows by 95, giving 78401 against the ceiling of 78401 in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`. `AGENTS.md` and the ratchet file are unchanged between the PR base and `main`. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` both concluded success on this head. Right, with zero headroom left (N3).
- Check-runs on the head: every run is success or skipped except the first `Check Changeset` run (started 23:14:16Z, failure), which a later run (23:17:21Z, skipped) supersedes; see ②.

### ② Semver level

- Nothing is published: the diff touches no package, so no changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` is the correct carrier.
- The first `Check Changeset` run failed because it ran before the label was on the PR. The run after the label concluded skipped, which is the job-level exemption `lint.yml` gives a `skip-changeset` PR. The failure is stale and is not a gate verdict on the labelled head.
- `Clause-②: no` is correct: no accept-set is widened and no public surface grows. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag 1 (is comment 7031931263 the record to cite for the weekly-card route): answered, the citation holds. I read the comment: it is on the card whose PR landed the weekly-card rule, and its row 2 states the rule ("an ADR amendment request appends a row to the open ADR revisions, week of … card … only ADR text that contradicts `main` is collected") with the maintainer's word 「adr接受你的建议」. No comment carrying a `Ruling:` line exists for that word, so a comment that carries the word together with the rule is the best available provenance. One correction to the PR body, not to the tree: it is not the earliest such comment (N2).
- Dev flag 2 (repo-wide tests and lint not run locally): answered by the check-runs; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Test UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success on this head.
- `open_questions`: empty.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff contains no code and no query.
- Ruling record 6797014134, read: letter B excludes `docs/adr/**` from an implementation card's file surface and has the landing seat file the ADR line after the merge, citing the merge commit. The moved citation now sits on the clause that record decided (the PR leaves `docs/adr/**` untouched). The filing destination that record named (its own `domain:skills` card) is the part the later word replaces, and the row no longer attributes the destination to it. Consistent.

### ④ Design judgment

`AGENTS.md`, the `packages/services/**` row, judged against the two cited records, the skill text on `main`, and the first weekly card as first consumer.

- Agreement with the skill on `main`: `execution-duties.md` says the landing seat, after the merge, appends one row (ADR, section, what it says, what is true now, landing PR) to the open weekly card and opens next week's card if none is open. The row says the same thing in the same order. The two routes that the card reported (own card in `AGENTS.md`, weekly row in the skill) become one. Holds.
- Collection rule: the skill collects only ADR text that contradicts `main`. A package name that differs from the ADR's proposal is such a contradiction by construction, so the row never sends a pure addition to the weekly card. Holds.
- First consumer: the first weekly card describes its rows as "ADR, section, what it says, what is true now, the landing PR" and lands them as append-only dated notes in one governed `docs/adr/**` PR. A row written from this rule fits that card. The old wording "status-line amendment" is gone, which is correct: the weekly card does not rewrite the status line. Holds.
- Attempt to break it, no open card: the first weekly card is closed today. The row covers this ("opening next week's if none is"), as the skill does. Holds.
- Attempt to break it, precedence: `AGENTS.md` outranks the skill. After this change the higher file no longer contradicts the lower one, and nothing else in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/**` on `main` still names the own-card route for this case (searched for "status-line amendment" and for the weekly card's title). Holds.
- Attempt to break it, the rows-only rule for `AGENTS.md`: the row carries no date, no quotation and no issue number; both provenance citations are ruling-record comment ids, the form the file's own header requires. Holds.

Findings:

- N1 (nit) — the row lists six fields, adding "merge commit" to the five the skill and the first weekly card name. It is a superset, the card asked for it, and the previous wording already required citing the merge commit. A seat following either text writes a row the weekly card accepts. Accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — the PR body says 7031931263 is the earliest comment carrying the maintainer's word with the rule. Comment 7030693413 (the triage comment on the card that first filed the rule) is earlier and carries the same word with the same rule. The citation in the tree is still sound: 7031931263 is on the card whose PR landed the rule, and states the rule as a row. No change to the tree is needed.
- N3 (nit) — "opening next week's if none is" drops the word "open" to fit the byte ceiling; it reads correctly next to "the open … card". The file now sits at the ceiling with zero headroom, so the next edit to `AGENTS.md` must remove bytes or bring a ruling that raises the ceiling. Follow-up at the seat's discretion.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

On the two header values. The security line reads no: the hunk teaches card routing only; no permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The rule-change line reads yes: `AGENTS.md` is not under `.claude/**`, so the queue guard does not read that line and the PR body declares no rule-change value; applied as written, the hunk does change what a landing seat does (a row on the weekly card in place of its own card) and what reaches the maintainer (one weekly approval in place of one per card), and the PR body has no ruling-ref line to check a copy against, so neither of the other two values is available. The PR waits for the maintainer in any case: `AGENTS.md` is Tier H.

- 落地条款:Tier H(AGENTS.md)。L2 PASS 在案,无未闭 must-fix/should-fix ⇒ 挂 `pm:awaiting-merge`、请 os-zhuang 审批;获批后席位过落地前检、摘标、ready、auto-merge。
